label: fiction
title: The Cancelled Drill
setting: The court sits in the present-day fictional state of Lydren. First Convenor Elian Voss was due to address an assembly at Neryn Hall before a close vote on emergency housing powers. A safety rehearsal involving green drill cards had been cancelled forty-eight hours earlier. Venue technician Sera Kelm entered the east gallery on the event day carrying one old card and a sealed instrument case. Security stopped the event before the Convenor entered the hall. No one was physically injured.
charge: attempting a terrorist assassination of the head of government
elements: The accused intended to kill the fictional head of government.
The accused took an act that went beyond mere preparation.
The accused intended the attack to intimidate the public or coerce the fictional government for an ideological purpose.
hook: The safety drill was cancelled, yet Sera Kelm arrived with its green authority card and a sealed case. Inside was a functional handgun. The jury must decide whether she was carrying out a lethal political plan or unknowingly finishing a confused technical handover.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: The drill was cancelled in writing, and Sera read that notice. Even so, she collected a sealed case from an unlisted locker, used an expired green card to enter the gallery, and directed a technician to mark the Convenor's speaking position. The case held a functional handgun. On the card's reverse, Sera had written that one fall before the vote would make every district understand. Those connected acts were not rehearsal work. They were the interrupted execution of an ideological assassination plan.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: Public events do not stop changing simply because one rehearsal is cancelled. Sera was told that a technical walk-through remained, collected what looked like the same sealed optics case used in earlier drills, and never opened it. The green card was old but familiar. The prosecution cannot date the dramatic sentence on its reverse, and the examiner cannot identify its writer conclusively. Sera's imprecise work decisions deserve criticism. They do not prove that she knew a handgun was present or intended anyone's death.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Follow what Sera knew and what she did after learning it. She acknowledged the cancellation, bypassed the updated issue desk, named a rehearsal that no supervisor had authorised, and placed the sealed case at the exact position she had Pellen mark for the Convenor. The case carried a fresh label strongly corresponding to Sera's writing. Her card carried a sentence linking a fall to the pending vote. Each fact answers the same question: this was a deliberate attempt to kill and frighten the public into political submission.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The prosecution's story becomes certain only by stripping every ambiguity from ordinary event work. Pellen assumed the walk-through concerned the Convenor; Sera said it concerned lighting. Davi cannot say who put the handgun in the sealed case. The replacement label proves Sera handled the case, which she admits, but not that she saw inside it. The sentence on a reusable card has no date and only a qualified handwriting opinion. Suspicion is profound. A grave charge still requires proof beyond reasonable doubt.

jurors.label: Yara
jurors.persona: Feels the danger of the recovered weapon but insists on proving Sera knew what was sealed inside.

agree: A handgun at that position is frightening, but fear cannot tell us what Sera knew.
pushback: The seal was intact. Which fact gets us from carrying the case to knowing its contents?
concede: The false drill claim and fresh label make an innocent handover much harder to accept.
burden_drift: Because security stopped it in time, I catch myself demanding that Sera explain the whole plot.
burden_correct: No. Prevention did not move the burden; the prosecution still proves intent.
holdout: I will not turn the weapon's presence into automatic knowledge.
final: I rely on Sera's deliberate disguise and false access story, not on the shock of what was inside.

jurors.label: Kel
jurors.persona: Separates chaotic event practice from conduct that specifically manufactured authority.

agree: Late changes happen. Inventing a restarted drill is not the same thing.
pushback: A reused card explains possession, but why announce a Convenor-route check?
concede: Pellen admits the marker served lighting too. That fact alone proves little.
burden_drift: The improvised label makes me want Sera to produce the missing caller.
burden_correct: She does not have to. We test whether her account leaves a reasonable doubt.
holdout: I need the acts to fit one purpose, not merely look irregular.
final: The fabricated authority, altered label, and placement fit deliberate access too precisely for me to dismiss.

jurors.label: Nima
jurors.persona: Refuses to let political language replace proof of the charged ideological purpose.

agree: The judge excluded general advocacy. We decide from this event's words and acts only.
pushback: Can the undated sentence prove present purpose without the case-specific conduct?
concede: Joined to the fresh false label and the invented drill, the sentence acquires a much narrower meaning.
burden_drift: The public stakes make uncertainty feel irresponsible, which is not a legal test.
burden_correct: The greater the allegation, the more carefully we keep the ordinary burden in place.
holdout: I will not convict a viewpoint; I need an intended killing and an intended coercive message.
final: The contemporaneous disguise and positioning prove those intentions without relying on excluded beliefs.

jurors.label: Oss
jurors.persona: Trusts physical continuity and pays close attention to what an intact seal cannot prove.

agree: Davi preserved the case properly, so we know what arrived in the gallery.
pushback: Good custody after recovery does not show what Sera knew before recovery.
concede: The label is different: fresh ink tied to Sera can reveal a deliberate disguise.
burden_drift: The sealed case feels like something only Sera can explain.
burden_correct: Silence cannot fill the knowledge element for the prosecution.
holdout: I need evidence around the seal, because the seal itself points both ways.
final: The false label and access story supply the knowledge that the closed case alone could not.

jurors.label: Vela · foreperson
jurors.persona: Keeps the room on three separate intentions and asks for a complete chronology.

agree: Let's map it: cancellation, locker, false restart, marker, gallery, then recovery.
pushback: Which step proves killing, and which proves the intended political message?
concede: The card sentence gains force because Sera carried it while making the matching event happen.
burden_drift: A missing innocent explanation can start sounding like a prosecution fact.
burden_correct: Sera's account may fail and the prosecution can still fall short. Those are separate questions.
holdout: I want every element tied to an admitted fact or a supported inference.
final: The connected sequence proves conduct beyond preparation and both charged intentions for me.

jurors.label: Bren
jurors.persona: Recognises the humane truth of Sera's working life and tests whether it explains the event-day choices.

agree: Sera's lawful career is real, and rushed managers genuinely did confuse crews.
pushback: But a good work history cannot answer why she created authority she knew had expired.
concede: Her admission that she overstated the task makes Pellen's account easier to trust.
burden_drift: I keep thinking a careful technician should prove how this went so wrong.
burden_correct: Carelessness is not charged, and Sera is not required to prove it.
holdout: I am still testing whether workplace chaos reasonably explains all three odd choices.
final: It explains one choice at a time, but not the combined false drill, label, and placement.

jurors.label: Lumi
jurors.persona: Moves when separate innocent-looking acts form a single event-specific design.

agree: A marker, card, and case each belong in ordinary venue work.
pushback: What are the odds all three innocent uses depended on the same invented restart?
concede: The sequence matters more than any dramatic object. Sera created the path from locker to marked position.
burden_drift: Once the pattern looks deliberate, I am tempted to ignore each weak link.
burden_correct: We still have to test the seal and the card date instead of smoothing them away.
holdout: Show me a complete prosecution sequence that keeps the limitations visible.
final: I have moved because the independent acts converge without needing the weapon itself to prove knowledge.

jurors.label: Teren
jurors.persona: Focuses on witness precision and resists converting Pellen's assumptions into Sera's words.

agree: Pellen distinguished the marker's ordinary use from Sera's unusual description.
pushback: Did Sera name a weapon or attack, or are we extending the phrase 'Convenor route'?
concede: The fresh label provides separate conduct that supports Pellen's interpretation.
burden_drift: Pellen sounded careful, and that can make every inference feel proved.
burden_correct: A credible witness can still supply only part of the case.
holdout: I will preserve the difference between words heard and meaning inferred.
final: Pellen's exact account, corroborated by the label and location, supports the charged meaning.

jurors.label: Sola
jurors.persona: Starts from public fear, then corrects herself when fear begins doing evidentiary work.

agree: People in that hall could have witnessed a killing. I feel the scale of that threat.
pushback: The event was stopped. We still need proof of what Sera meant, not just what could have happened.
concede: Her sentence connects the intended fall to the vote, which addresses the public purpose.
burden_drift: Part of me wants certainty that the hall is safe more than certainty that Sera is guilty.
burden_correct: Community safety cannot lower beyond reasonable doubt for this accused.
holdout: I need to decide the event before us, not the danger in the abstract.
final: The event-specific words and acts persuade me without using public fear as a shortcut.

jurors.label: Jori
jurors.persona: Treats the missing voice message as possible but asks whether it can explain the surrounding details.

agree: Temporary crew messages really did disappear, so the absence does not prove invention.
pushback: Would an innocent caller also tell Sera to alter a label and claim a cancelled drill had resumed?
concede: The supposed instruction is possible, but it does not account for the whole route.
burden_drift: I want the defence to find the caller because that would settle my unease.
burden_correct: The prosecution must exclude the innocent message reasonably; Sera need not locate it.
holdout: I am leaving room for flawed systems until the other evidence closes it.
final: The message possibility remains, but the deliberate false authority makes it unreasonable in this sequence.

jurors.label: Evin
jurors.persona: Tests whether each element is independently established rather than inferred from the seriousness of the charge.

agree: Knowing the case was dangerous is not identical to intending the Convenor's death.
pushback: Where is the ideological purpose if we set the undated sentence aside?
concede: The sentence need not stand alone; Sera carried it while staging the event it describes.
burden_drift: Three suspicious intentions can blur into one general feeling of guilt.
burden_correct: We must be sure of killing, action beyond preparation, and coercive purpose separately.
holdout: I am checking the proof against each element before combining the inferences.
final: The marked position proves action, the disguised case proves knowledge, and the card supplies the intended public message.

accused.human: Sera Kelm, 34, has spent twelve years making public halls safe for performers, school groups, and civic meetings. She supports her father through weekly visits and mentors two apprentice technicians. Colleagues knew her as meticulous about labels, though impatient when event managers changed plans without updating crews.

beats.text: The event schedule fixed the First Convenor's address for 14:30 beneath the east-gallery clock. An authorised safety drill had once been planned for the same room, using green cards to identify participating technicians, but the venue manager cancelled it by group notice forty-eight hours before the address. Sera opened that notice at 09:12 the next morning and replied, 'Understood.' A separate lighting check remained on the calendar, without gallery access or sealed equipment. These agreed records establish the setting and Sera's knowledge of the cancellation, not her later purpose.
beats.speaker: pc

beats.text: Pellen, what work did you expect at Neryn Hall that afternoon? Only a lighting check from the floor. The safety drill, gallery sweep, and mock arrival had all been cancelled. What did Sera tell you when she arrived? She said the east-gallery walk-through was back on and asked me to mark where the Convenor would stand beneath the clock. Did you have authority to restart that drill? No. I trusted Sera because she had supervised previous rehearsals, so I placed a removable floor marker and returned downstairs.

beats.text: Pellen, had you seen Sera at public meetings about the emergency housing powers? Yes. She spoke against the proposal and urged officials to withdraw it, but she remained calm and attended openly. Defence counsel objected before the prosecution could use lawful advocacy as evidence of a lethal purpose. The judge excluded the entire exchange and directed the jury to disregard it.

interjections.speaker: dc
interjections.text: Objection. Lawful public advocacy does not prove that Sera intended this charged act.

interjections.speaker: judge
interjections.text: Sustained. Disregard this entire exchange. Lawful political advocacy is not evidence of guilt or terrorist purpose.

beats.text: The handwritten sentence is admitted only as evidence that may bear on Sera's knowledge, intention, and alleged purpose when considered with the fresh case label and her conduct. It is not proof that she acted merely because the words sound political. General speeches, lawful advocacy, associations, and opinions have been excluded from this trial. You must not speculate about them or treat unpopular belief as criminal character. The prosecution must prove the case-specific intention charged here from admissible acts and words connected to this event.
beats.speaker: judge

beats.text: Sera, why did you go to the east gallery? A voice message from someone I believed was the deputy manager said the technical walk-through still needed an east-angle check. Why use the green card and collect that case? The old card was still in my kit, and locker fourteen was where optics had been staged in earlier drills. I thought the case held a lens. Did you write the sentence about a fall before the vote? I wrote something like it months earlier while helping a community theatre scene about a collapsing government. I did not mean a person's death.

beats.text: The prosecution must prove every element beyond reasonable doubt. Intending death is different from carelessness, alarm, or knowledge that a dangerous object was nearby. An attempt requires an act beyond mere preparation, but the act need not be the final possible step. Terrorist purpose requires an intention to intimidate the public or coerce government for an ideological end; lawful opinion is irrelevant. Consider the false-restart evidence, the case, the label, the card sentence, and their limits together. Sera need not prove the voice message existed or identify who packed the case. If an innocent explanation remains reasonably possible on any element, return Not Guilty. Do not research the case or the technical subjects online.
